nodes.name: CoFe PBA precipitation
nodes.procedure: The sum of 0.6 mmol CoCl2·6H2O and additional 0.9 mmol trisodium citrate dehydrate (TCD) were dissolved in 20 mL of deionized water to form solution A. Second, 0.4 mmol of K3[Fe(CN)6] was dissolved in 20 mL of deionized water to form solution B. Subsequently, solution A was poured slowly into stirring solution B and mixed them sufficiently. After stirring for 10 min, the mixture was placed at room temperature for 48 h without any disturbance. Finally, after the centrifugation process proceeded for 10 min at 8000 rpm, the precipitate was concomitantly washed with deionized water and ethanol three times, respectively, followed by drying at 60 °C for 24 h to harvest the final product of CoFe PBA.

nodes.name: CoP/FeP phosphating
nodes.procedure: 100 mg of the as-synthesized CoFe PBA and 500 mg of sodium hypophosphite were placed at both ends of the porcelain boat for continuous calcining under an Ar atmosphere at 450 °C for 2 h at a heating rate of 2 °C min⁻¹. Therein, sodium hypophosphite was placed in the inlet position of the airflow in the tubular furnace. The samples of CoP/FeP were taken out after the reaction mixture was cooled down to room temperature.

nodes.source_text: The electrocatalytic performance of Sn-CoP/FeP was evaluated by using a standard three-electrode system in 1 M KOH aqueous solution with a SCE as the reference electrode and a graphite rod as the counter electrode... To reach a current density of 10 mA cm⁻², Sn-CoP/FeP required an overpotential (η₁₀) of only 62 mV... The Tafel slope of Sn-CoP/FeP was determined to be 71 mV dec⁻¹... charge transfer resistance (R_ct) of 10.6 Ω... C_dl value of Sn-CoP/FeP was calculated to be 42.43 mF cm⁻²... remain stable after continuous operation for 35 h... nearly 100% faradaic efficiency... after 1000 CV cycles, the LSV curve... exhibited a negligible negative shift

CoP/FeP (111 mV)... Tafel slope... CoP/FeP (88 mV dec⁻¹)... R_ct... CoP/FeP (33.7 Ω)... C_dl... CoP/FeP (23.49 mF cm⁻²)... faradaic efficiency of Sn-CoP/FeP (100%)... superior to that of CoP/FeP (95%)... CoP/FeP... displayed slight decay after long-term operation
Sn-CoFe PBA (245 mV)... Tafel slope... Sn-CoFe PBA (95 mV dec⁻¹)... R_ct... Sn-CoFe PBA (396 Ω)... C_dl... Sn-CoFe PBA (12.02 mF cm⁻²)
CoFe PBA (266 mV)... Tafel slope... CoFe PBA (107 mV dec⁻¹)... R_ct... CoFe PBA (421 Ω)... C_dl... CoFe PBA (10.42 mF cm⁻²)
competitive to the benchmark Pt/C catalyst... Pt/C 33 mV... TOF of Sn-CoP/FeP was calculated to be 12.62 s⁻¹ at an overpotential of 200 mV, comparable with that of Pt/C (9.89 s⁻¹)

the electrocatalytic performance of Sn-CoP/FeP was also investigated in 0.5 M H₂SO₄ solution using a Pt plate or a carbon rod as the counter electrode, respectively. The result suggested that the HER activity of Sn-CoP/FeP is consistent with the case under alkaline conditions and the counter electrode could not influence the HER performance either in 1 M KOH or 0.5 M H₂SO₄

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM image reveals Sn-CoFe PBA (Co²⁺/Sn²⁺ = 2:1) exhibits distorted Archimedean polyhedron consisting of corner-cut square from (100) plane and triangle-shape surface from (111) facet.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1a, the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image revealed that the Sn-CoFe PBA prepared with a Co²⁺/Sn²⁺ ratio of 2 : 1 exhibited a distorted Archimedean polyhedron consisting of a corner-cut square derived from the (100) plane of the CoFe PBA cube and a triangle-shape surface from the (111) facet of CoFe PBA

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms Sn-CoFe PBA (Co²⁺/Sn²⁺ = 2:1) possesses corner-cut polyhedron structure with smooth surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) (Fig. 1b) image confirmed that Sn-CoFe PBA possessed a corner-cut polyhedron structure and well maintained the smooth surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED shows discrete spots indexed to (200), (220), and (400) planes indicating single crystal structure similar to CoFe PBA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) (Fig. S2a†) showing discrete spots indexed to the (200), (220), and (400) planes

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM discloses interplanar crystal spacing of 0.501 nm corresponding to (200) plane, slightly smaller than 0.506 nm of CoFe PBA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image (Fig. S2b†) disclosed an interplanar crystal spacing of 0.501 nm corresponding to the (200) plane

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows peaks at 31.86°, 36.45°, 48.22°, 56.57° for CoP (011), (111), (211), (301) facets and 32.73°, 46.99°, 48.36° for FeP (011), (220), (211) planes; peaks slightly down-shifted due to Sn insertion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the peaks located at 31.86°, 36.45°, 48.22°, and 56.57° were assigned to the (011), (111), (211), and (301) facets of orthorhombic CoP (PDF no. 29-0497), respectively. The peaks at 32.73°, 46.99°, and 48.36° were ascribed to the (011), (220), and (211) planes of orthorhombic FeP (PDF no. 71-2262)

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area of Sn-CoP/FeP is 20.31 m²/g, larger than CoP/FeP at 13.68 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area of Sn-CoP/FeP (20.31 m² g⁻¹) was much larger than that of its counterpart CoP/FeP (13.68 m² g⁻¹)

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Co 2p: Co³⁺ (778.79, 793.84 eV), Co²⁺ (780.71, 797.57 eV); Fe 2p: Fe²⁺ (708.52, 721.37 eV), Fe³⁺ (713.03, 725.47 eV); Sn 3d: Sn²⁺ (487.41, 495.84 eV), Sn-Co/Fe (485.71 eV); P 2p: Co-P/Fe-P (129.24, 130.22 eV), oxidized P (133.71 eV). Positive shift in Co/Fe binding energies indicates charge transfer induced by Sn²⁺.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the high-resolution XPS spectrum of Co 2p (Fig. 3c), it was found that the peaks located at 778.79 and 793.84 eV were attributed to the 2p₃/₂ and 2p₁/₂ splitting of Co³⁺ in CoP... the positive shift of the binding energy for Co²⁺/Co³⁺ and Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺ in Sn-CoP/FeP indicates that the charge transfer from Co/Fe to P induced by Sn²⁺ was occurred

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows D band at 1366 cm⁻¹ and G band at 1586 cm⁻¹ confirming graphitic carbon.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peaks at 1366 and 1586 cm⁻¹ could be ascribed to the D and G bands

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-IR shows new peak at 2160 cm⁻¹ ascribed to Coᴵᴵ-C≡N-Feᴵᴵᴵ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a new peak observed at 2160 cm⁻¹ in the Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectrum of Sn-CoFe PBA... which was ascribed to Coᴵᴵ-C≡N-Feᴵᴵᴵ

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP test indicates negligible release of Sn and P ions after cyclic voltammetry.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP test indicated that the release of Sn and P ions to the solution of Sn-CoP/FeP after cyclic voltammetry measurements can be ignored.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows charge transfer resistance (R_ct) of 10.6 Ω for Sn-CoP/FeP, smaller than CoP/FeP (33.7 Ω).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Nyquist curves shown in Fig. 4d disclosed a much smaller semi-circle for Sn-CoP/FeP with a favorable charge transfer resistance (R_ct) of 10.6 Ω, superior to those of CoP/FeP (33.7 Ω)

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in non-Faradaic region gives double layer capacitance (C_dl) of 42.43 mF/cm² for Sn-CoP/FeP, indicating larger ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the C_dl value of Sn-CoP/FeP was calculated to be 42.43 mF cm⁻², larger than those of CoP/FeP (23.49 mF cm⁻²)
